![What's new in cheek 0.2.0](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Mailo037/cheek/v0.2.0/docs/releases/v0.2.0.png)

cheek 0.2.0 writes covers and tags into every file, resumes HLS and DASH fragment downloads and picks formats straight from `--info-json`.

- `--embed-thumbnail` puts the thumbnail into the file as its cover: an attached picture in MP4, M4A, MOV, MP3 and FLAC, an attachment in MKV and a picture block in Opus and Ogg comments. WebP thumbnails become JPEG first. A thumbnail that can't be fetched doesn't fail the download.
- `--embed-metadata` writes title, artist and link even into files that needed no other ffmpeg step, such as an M4A that was already M4A. That step reports the new `tagging` stage.
- Interrupted HLS and DASH fragment downloads continue from the last fragment written, also when a new resolve brings new tokens for the same fragments.
- With `--info-json`, `-f` now picks from the JSON's formats by yt-dlp's rules, so one resolve serves every quality without starting yt-dlp again.
- Cineby and CineSrc links (`cinesrc:movie:TMDB_ID`, `cinesrc:tv:TMDB_ID:SEASON:EPISODE`, embed, `/movie/` and `/watch/` links) resolve on desktop through a temporary headless Chrome, Chromium or Edge session, without your browser profile or cookies. `--resolver yt-dlp` skips it.

Includes binaries for Linux, Windows, macOS and all three Android ABIs used by Hamstr. Verify downloads against `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
